articles.title: Schools shut, relief measures intensified in three North Andhra districts as cyclone nears - The Hindu

articles.full_text:
M. Abhishikth Kishore, District Collector Visakhapatnam
| Photo Credit: V RAJU
The district administrations of Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli and Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) have stepped up precautionary measures ahead of Cyclone Arnab, for which the India Meteorological Department has issued a red alert.
Visakhapatnam Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore said; “All educational institutions would remain closed on Tuesday and Wednesday.” He ordered the closure of beaches and advised people to avoid tourist spots and to step out only in emergencies. A National Disaster Response Force team and a State Disaster Response Force team are stationed in the district. The Navy and the Coast Guard have also been alerted. Relief camps are being readied, and pregnant women nearing their due dates are being identified for shifting to hospitals. Accompanied by Joint Collector G. Vidyadhari, he inspected the district control room and asked officials to brief the media every six hours. Control rooms have been opened at the Collectorate (0891-2590100, 0891-2590102) and in the tahsildars’ offices of all 11 mandals. Special officers have been assigned to each mandal.
Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation Commissioner Ketan Garg has asked residents of low-lying and hilly areas to remain vigilant and stay indoors for three days, barring emergencies. Help is available on 1800 4250 0009 and on WhatsApp number at 9014218870.
Andhra University has cancelled in-person classes from Monday and will hold them online until November 4, Registrar K. Rambabu said.
Vijaya Krishnan, District Collector Anakapalli
| Photo Credit:
KR DEEPAK
In Anakapalli, Collector Vijaya Krishnan declared a holiday for schools of all managements from October 27 to 29. At a video conference, she directed officials to start flood stores and relief centres in six coastal mandals from Monday night and to move residents of kutcha houses, huts and tin sheds to safer places. A team with a JCB, a tipper and 10 workers is to be kept ready for every 5 km of road. The Eastern Power Distribution Company has opened a round-the-clock control room (8712410720), and the Agriculture Department has one from October 27 to 31 to advise farmers. Handloom and Textiles Department officer Padma has asked weavers to cover looms, yarn and finished cloth with tarpaulins, shift stocks to dry places and keep electrical fittings dry.
T. Nishanthi, District Collector, Alluri Sitharama Raju district
| Photo Credit:
th-online Administrator
In the ASR district, Collector T. Nishanthi announced a holiday on Tuesday and Wednesday for day-scholar schools, colleges and anganwadi centres. Residential schools and hostels will continue to function. A 24-hour control room has been set up at the Collectorate (08935-293448). At a teleconference, the Collector directed officials to keep medical personnel, medicines and ambulances ready, with special attention to patients and pregnant women, and to monitor the situation round the clock through control rooms at district and mandal levels. Raincoats and satellite phones will be provided to personnel on cyclone duty and on ZPTC and MPTC election duty. ITDA Project Officer Aditya Varma has asked officials to shift residents of landslide-prone areas to safer locations.
The State government has released ₹27 crore to 20 districts for relief operations. Special Chief Secretary (Disaster Management) G. Sai Prasad issued orders allotting ₹2 crore each to Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, Konaseema, East Godavari, Kakinada and Anakapalli, and ₹1 crore each to Srikakulam, Markapuram, Guntur, NTR, Eluru, ASR, Polavaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Sri Sathya Sai, Nellore and Tirupati.
Published - October 26, 2026 10:07 pm IST

articles.title: ‘Arnab’ to cross Andhra coast on Wednesday as a very severe cyclonic storm - Deccan Herald

Hyderabad: The severe low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclonic Storm ‘Arnab’, and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert. On Monday evening, the system lay over the west-central and adjoining east-central Bay of Bengal after moving west-northwestwards at 13 km per hour over the previous six hours. It was centred about 520 km southeast of Gopalpur (Odisha), 540 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 620 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 720 km east-southeast of Machilipatnam and 790 km east-southeast of Bapatla, as well as 680 km northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman Islands.

The IMD said the storm is very likely to continue moving west-northwestwards and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by late Monday evening, and into a very severe cyclonic storm over the same region on Tuesday. It is then expected to turn northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam and close to Yanam, by the forenoon of October 28.

At landfall, it is expected to be a very severe cyclonic storm with maximum sustained winds of 115-125 km per hour, gusting to 140 km per hour. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has advised people to remain alert on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday.

.Tamil Nadu rains: 14 killed in lightning strikes, tourist entry barred to hill stations.

Gale winds of 90-100 km per hour, gusting to 110 km per hour, are expected over the west-central and adjoining east-central Bay of Bengal by Tuesday midnight. Winds are likely to strengthen to 115-125 km per hour, gusting to 140 km per hour, from Wednesday afternoon until landfall. After landfall, they are expected to ease to 60-70 km per hour, gusting to 80 km per hour, by Wednesday evening, and to squally winds of 40-50 km per hour, gusting to 60 km per hour, by Thursday morning, before decreasing gradually.

Moderate to heavy rainfall is expected in several districts from Srikakulam to Nellore from Tuesday afternoon, accompanied by strong winds along the coast. Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is likely on October 28 and 29 in the North Coastal Andhra districts, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, NTR, Guntur, Palnadu, Bapatla, Prakasam and Nellore.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and senior officials are monitoring the cyclone’s movement and have alerted the districts likely to bear the brunt. Naidu directed officials in the coastal districts to take all precautionary measures in advance and to keep the Central Government informed of the steps being taken.

He ordered comprehensive measures to prevent loss of life and property. People living in flood-prone and low-lying areas must be moved to cyclone shelters, with priority given to the elderly, persons with disabilities, pregnant women and infants. Officials said arrangements were under way to shift 4,711 identified pregnant women to Primary Health Centres, Community Health Centres and hospitals. The Chief Minister directed that medical teams and ambulances be kept ready at health centres in the affected districts.

Seven National Disaster Response Force teams and eight State Disaster Response Force teams are to be deployed across 11 vulnerable districts, with additional forces on standby in NTR and Visakhapatnam districts. Naidu also asked officials to coordinate with the Marine Police, Navy and Coast Guard so that their services are available for rescue and relief operations.

Officials reported that all fishermen who had ventured out to sea have returned safely, with 30,043 boats reaching harbours. The Chief Minister instructed that fishermen should not go to sea until the cyclone weakens and normal conditions return.

The Agriculture Department has been told to move harvested paddy to safe locations and to take precautionary measures to protect horticultural crops spread over about 1.82 lakh hectares. Naidu also asked officials to ensure adequate stocks of essential commodities at ration shops and to restore electricity supply immediately wherever it is disrupted.

Officials expect the Tandava, Raiwada, Yeleru, Tammileru, Yerrakalava and Tadipudi reservoirs to receive inflows up to their full storage capacities. The Chief Minister directed that streams, rivulets and canals be kept free of obstructions to allow smooth flow of water. District collectors have been told to take strict action against those spreading misinformation about the cyclone on social media, and to assess the likely impact on individual areas and declare holidays for educational institutions where necessary.

articles.full_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a top-priority Red Message (Cyclone Warning) for the coasts of Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha as Cyclonic Storm “Arnab” (pronounced Ornab) rapidly intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal on Monday evening.
As of 17:30 hrs IST on October 26, 2026, the severe storm was centered near latitude 15.6°N and longitude 87.3°E. Moving west-northwestwards at a speed of 17 kmph over the preceding six hours, the cyclone is currently situated:
490 km south-southeast of Gopalpur (Odisha)
490 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh)
560 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh)
660 km east of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh)
730 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh)
730 km northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands)
Trajectory and Expected Landfall
Meteorologists project that Cyclone Arnab will continue its west-northwestward path while intensifying further into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm within the next 12 hours over the same region.
The system is forecasted to maintain its west-northwestward movement until the evening of October 27, before re-curving slightly towards the northwest. It is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam—passing close to Yanam—as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm by the forenoon of October 28, 2026. During landfall, maximum sustained wind speeds are predicted to reach 115–125 kmph, gusting up to 140 kmph.
Alerts and Disaster Preparedness
With the Red Alert activated, coastal authorities in Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry (Yanam), and Odisha have been advised to brace for severe weather conditions. Fishermen have been strictly instructed to return to land and avoid venturing into the central and western Bay of Bengal until landfall operations subside.
Local administrations are mobilizing response units, including National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams, in low-lying coastal areas susceptible to heavy rainfall, coastal inundation, and strong storm surges.
Residents in vulnerable zones are urged to stay informed through official weather bulletins and follow instructions from local authorities.
Yajati K. Rout is a dynamic journalist at Pragativadi, known for delivering nuanced and impactful storytelling that spans Odisha’s societal fabric to global sports arenas. His reporting navigates seamlessly between grassroots realities, high-profile political developments, and the pulse of international tennis and cricket.
